description: Haarlemmerdijk / Haarlemmerstraat narrow gable shop houses (17th-18th c. fronts, many BAG-dated to 19th-20th c. rebuilds): 3.6-6.2 m fronts of dark red-brown brick, a tall shop ground storey to about 4.7 m and two upper storeys (about 3.0 and 2.4 m) of white-framed T-windows, under a neck gable with one attic light, a bell gable, or a plain point gable rising 2.3-3.5 m over a gable foot at about 10 m

match.note: Haarlemmerdijk 2-26 (2022-12-15 strip, 1 m grid): shop fascia top 4.6-4.9 m, window rows 5.7-7.6 and 8.2-9.7 m, gable foot 10.0-10.3 m; neck tops 12.9-13.2 m (necks 1.4-1.6 m wide), point gable of 8 to 14.3 m. 3DBAG eaves for the same fronts read 7.1-10.3 m (rear roofs), so the eaves criterion is weak here; the skyline crown decides between this type and the cornice house. crownStrict off: on the narrow dijk the fused strip carries ghost gables of the neighbours (2022-12-15), so the skyline crown is a score, and reviewer crown pins decide. crownMatch off and eavesM [9.6, 12.0] (a 3.6 m pitch: three storeys at 9.8-11.6 m, four at 12.4-14.4 m, the tall shop ground counted in): every placed pand on these faces carries a reviewer type and crown pin, and eaves pins from the 1 m grid

neck.note: Haarlemmerdijk 20 (167818): neck 10.2-12.9 m, 1.55 m wide, one attic light 10.4-11.6 m, scrolls not drawn

bell.note: Haarlemmerdijk 4 (176174): a bell/neck top about 10.3-12.8 m with one attic light

point.note: Haarlemmerdijk 8 (176101): a plain brick point gable 10.4-14.3 m over the full front with two attic lights

door-left.note: residential ground: house door on the left axis; shops come per pand from BAG/OSM (autoShopfront)

rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: a shop (BAG/OSM) or a house door and window | upper: 2 or 3
rhythm.groundFloor: a tall shop ground 4.4-4.9 m to the fascia top on the dijk and straat
rhythm.roofline: neck, bell or point gable with one or two attic lights
